label: Required by a being's own end: y's own good could not be had without x (a primitive)
term: required by a being's end (the EndRequires parameter)
definition: EndRequires y x, for beings y and x: x is required by y's own end, that is, the good that y's appetite (natural or rational) is ordered to could not be had without x. A primitive Lean parameter of type B → B → Prop of TruthCore.Causality.NarDerivation, constrained only by the open premises that use it: WN (RationalFixedGivingIsRequired, a rational power is fixed toward a given being only if that being is required by the giver's end) and SS (ActualRootsEndRequiresNoOther, no being other than an actual root is required by its end). No structural property (reflexivity, transitivity) is assumed; it is world-free, like the will bridges of #1941.
note: Analyst primitive, attribution deferred (docs/notes/nar-derivation.md). Intended reading: ST I q.19 a.3 co. and q.82 a.1 (navigation, not attributed): the will adheres of necessity to its last end and to what the end cannot be had without, as one wills of necessity to take food if one wills to live, but not to other means. Examples: an animal's flourishing requires food; a ship's voyage requires a ship. Non-examples: a generous person's goodness does not require the particular gifts given; on classical theism, God's goodness requires no creature ('His goodness can be without other things, ... no perfection can accrue to Him from them'). Distinct from causal or grounding dependence: x can be required by y's end without grounding or being grounded by y. OPEN semantic obligations: whether 'end' applies univocally to a first source; whether necessary diffusion of the good (Neoplatonism; Avicenna) counts as the end requiring its effects or as a fixity that WN's rival affirms without requirement (note section 5).
